parts:
Alright, well here's a reproducible example ^_^:

This is a trait that I mapped onto the tree and used "make.simmap" from "phylotools" for ancestral character reconstruction:

AcetylTrait <- setNames(OccupMatrix$Acetyl, OccupMatrix$Species)
AcetylTrait<- as.factor(AcetylTrait)
cols<-setNames(c("darkorange1","blue"), levels(AcetylTrait))
mtree<-make.simmap(BigProk.Tree,AcetylTrait,model="ER")
plot(mtree,cols,type="phylogram",ftype="off", lwd=0.4)

The tree and characters are plotting very well, like this:
  

Now, I have another tree that I want to compare to this one using the example that you provided here: http://yulab-smu.top/treedata-book/chapter2.html#ggtree-fortify (Figure 2.6)

Code used for the second tree:

nwk <- system.file("extdata", "AcetylTree.nwk", package="treeio")
Acetyl.Tree <- read.tree(nwk)
Acetyl.df<-arrange(as_tibble(Acetyl.Tree), desc(label))

metadata<-read.csv("Acetyl.csv", sep=";", header = TRUE)
Phyla<-c(metadata$lv2_group)
length(Phyla)<-length(Acetyl.df$label)
Acetyl.df.1<-tibble(Acetyl.df, Phyla)
grp<-tapply(Acetyl.df.1$label, Acetyl.df.1$Phyla, list)
AcetylTree<-groupOTU(Acetyl.Tree, grp, 'Phyla')

p<-ggtree(AcetylTree, aes(color=Phyla), ladderize=FALSE, size=0.2) + 
  theme(legend.position="right") +
  geom_tiplab(size=1, color="gray30") + 
  geom_rootedge(rootedge = 0.01, color ="tan") +
  geom_nodelab(size=1, color="brown") + 
  geom_nodepoint(size=0.1) +
  geom_text2(aes(subset=!isTip, label=node), size=0.1)

p

Libraries used:
library("treeio")
library("ggtree")
library("ape")
library("tidytree")
library("tibble")
library("ggplot2")
library("phytools")

R version: R version 4.0.2 (2020-06-22). RStudio version: 1.3.1073

Question: How do I plot the first tree against the second tree and compare them like in your example above (link was provided) since the first one is not a ggtree object?

Or, how can I visualize "mtree" with its mapped characters using ggtree? Because that would make plotting the trees against each other easy, because I can just follow your example.

Thank you for taking the time.

Ggtree is a terrific package!

anoletree is an example SIMMAP tree in phytools.
